jurisdiction._about: Every request is voluntary, under the broker's own published opt-out process: it claims no residency and no legal right. Your state is your current address's in Your details (two letters), or `states` when that has none. `checked` is the date (YYYY-MM-DD) you last looked at whether your state's law gives you a right to deletion; ./manage.py doctor reminds you after recheck_months.
jurisdiction._laws: When a law of your state that gives you a right to deletion takes effect, add it here: {"name": "<the law's name>", "state": "<your state's two letters>", "cite": "…", "effective": "YYYY-MM-DD", "covers": ["marketing", "people-search"]}. Requests to brokers it covers then use the deletion_rights template, which cites it, while you live in that state. Until then every request is voluntary.
jurisdiction._regulators: Where a complaint draft is filed. Add your state attorney general's complaint page, keyed by the state's two letters ("XX": "https://…"): a draft names it while you live in that state.

tiers.1: confirmed exposure: broker scripts on pages where you typed your email (the browser extension)
tiers.2: crucial people-search sites (the Big-Ass list's top tier)
tiers.3: the other people-search and background-check sites
tiers.5: the long tail of registered brokers, by email
